question: A clinical study evaluates a new antihypertensive medication. Among 40 patients who took the drug, 28 showed a reduction in systolic blood pressure of at least 10 mmHg. Calculate the lower bound of the 95% Wilson confidence interval for the true proportion of patients who would experience this reduction. Give your answer to 3 decimal places.
r_solution:
x <- 28
n <- 40
phat <- x/n
z <- qnorm(0.975)
den <- 1 + z^2/n
center <- (phat + z^2/(2*n))/den
margin <- (z * sqrt(phat*(1-phat)/n + z^2/(4*n^2)))/den
cat(center - margin)

question: A study in coastal hospitality examines whether a Green Stay certification is associated with higher guest ratings. The data from 350 stays are summarized in a 2x2 table. The number of stays with an Excellent rating is 120 for certified hotels and 45 for non-certified hotels. The number of stays with an Other rating is 80 for certified hotels and 105 for non-certified hotels. Construct the 95 percent confidence interval for the odds ratio of receiving an Excellent rating for certified versus non-certified hotels. To do this, compute the log odds ratio, add the standard normal quantile for 95 percent confidence multiplied by the standard error on the log scale (where the variance of the log odds ratio is the sum of the reciprocals of the four cell counts), and exponentiate the result. Give the upper bound of the interval to 3 decimal places.
r_solution:
a <- 120
b <- 80
c <- 45
d <- 105
or_val <- (a*d)/(b*c)
log_or <- log(or_val)
se <- sqrt(1/a + 1/b + 1/c + 1/d)
upper <- exp(log_or + qnorm(0.975) * se)
cat(upper)
